clue.text: Sacred writings in text for play sure to be altered

parts.note: the text of a play is its script

indicators.note: the word sure is to be changed in form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Holy texts are hidden in a playscript that is bound to be rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be altered' is the anagram signal for sure; 'in' is only a link word between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The scriptures are the holy books of a religion, especially the Bible.

clue.text: Allows for delivering supplies

definitions.meaning: to provide for something is to make allowance for it
to provide is to supply or furnish

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the same verb: making allowance for something, and furnishing goods.

clue.text: Sportsman's hat

definitions.meaning: a cricketer who delivers the ball
a hard round felt hat, the derby

explanation.definitionFit: A cricket player who bowls, and also the hard round hat associated with City gents.

clue.text: She would shortly take off

parts.note: taken as written
would in its shortened form is the contraction 'd, as in I'd

explanation.surface: A woman would soon fly away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' here means remove, as clothing or skin, not fly; the apostrophe of the contraction is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed clothes or a skin is to remove or cast them off.

clue.text: Expert takes one of the store's bargains first

annotationWithheld.why: Expert takes one of the store's bargains first: SPECIAL gives the first seven letters, but no clue word plainly supplies IST
annotationWithheld.clue: Expert takes one of the store's bargains first

clue.text: A type of column located initially by Liverpool railway engineer

parts.note: the spinal column is the backbone

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word located is taken

explanation.surface: A column found near a railway engineer from Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: John Aspinall was a locomotive engineer born in Liverpool, chief mechanical engineer of the Lancashire and Yorkshire Railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Aspinall was a nineteenth-century British locomotive engineer from Liverpool.

clue.text: It's sickening to quote me when rising

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters are read upward, i.e. backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: Quoting oneself while getting up is nauseating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when rising' turns CITE ME upward in this down light, giving EMETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance taken to induce vomiting.

clue.text: Unknown author to be revealed soon

definitions.meaning: an anonymous writer, abbreviated as used under unattributed works
an archaic word for shortly or presently

explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation marks a work of unknown authorship; the old adverb means in a little while.

clue.text: Nothing in remastered graphics shows carrier at sea

indicators.note: the round letter is placed inside the other letters
a remastered recording is reworked, so the letters of graphics are rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Upgraded computer graphics depict an empty vessel at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remastered' is the anagram signal, and 'Nothing' is zero, the round letter, which goes inside the rearranged letters; 'shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cargo vessel carries freight across the sea.

clue.text: Simpleton on way to fair possibly is coming back one day

definitions.text: Simpleton on way to fair possibly

indicators.note: the little word is is read backwards

parts.note: Mon is the short form of Monday

explanation.surface: A fool heading for the fair returns one day.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls the nursery rhyme 'Simple Simon met a pieman, going to the fair'. 'coming back' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the simple lad named here meets a pieman on his way to the fair.

clue.text: Wrong patient

definitions.meaning: stressed on the second syllable, not valid or incorrect
stressed on the first syllable, a person disabled by illness

explanation.definitionFit: Pronounced two ways, the word means either not valid or a sick, disabled person.

clue.text: 151 not out — nice start for ex-president

parts.note: in Roman numerals 151 is CLI

indicators.note: the word not is put out of order, so its letters are rearranged
only the opening letter of nice is used

explanation.surface: A cricket score of 151 not out is a fine beginning for a former president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges NOT to NTO; 'start' takes N from nice. The surface reads as a batsman's unbeaten score.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Clinton was the 42nd President of the United States.

clue.text: Tour planned to take daughter in to royal house

indicators.note: together with in, says one piece is taken inside the other
completes the containment instruction begun by to take
a planned tour is arranged, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tour is arranged to bring a daughter into a royal household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planned' rearranges TOUR to TUOR; 'to take ... in' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English royal dynasty from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Snowdrop found in the Alps?

parts.note: not the flower but a literal drop of snow falling down a mountainside

explanation.walkthrough: 'Snowdrop' wants to be the spring flower; read it as snow dropping down a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of snow sliding down a mountain is literally a drop of snow.

clue.text: A new gal Una negotiated yearly pay

indicators.note: terms that are negotiated are worked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two women bargained over their salary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiated' rearranges the letters of A NEW GAL UNA.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual wage is the pay earned over a year.

clue.text: The first woman gets online — to what part? All over the place

parts.note: in Genesis Eve is the first woman
on a line read as railway, abbreviated Ry
to what place is where

explanation.surface: Eve goes online and asks where she should go, then finds herself scattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link word; 'online' supplies RY, the abbreviation for railway, a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Something found all over the place is present in every location.

clue.text: About treating one with dental caries, as provided by nursing home

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the letters of these words are worked on and rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Treating someone with tooth decay, as a care home might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treating' signals the anagram of all three fodder words together; 'with' just joins them and 'as' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-term residential care is the accommodation and nursing a care home provides.

clue.text: Slim and wealthy? That could be Marlene

parts.note: to slim is to diet
wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: Being thin and rich might describe a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: Marlene Dietrich was a German-American film actress and singer.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the film star Marlene, famous for The Blue Angel.

clue.text: One not consumed — take note!

parts.note: an means one, as the indefinite article
consumed food was eaten, so ate

explanation.surface: Someone who has not eaten is told to pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To annotate a text is to add notes to it, writing down comments.

clue.text: Taking public transport back to worker after ten, he pays part of lease

indicators.note: the worker piece comes after ten
the word for the vehicle is read backwards

parts.note: a bus is public transport
taken as written
a worker ant, the stock crossword worker

explanation.surface: Taking the bus home to work after ten, someone pays part of the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals reversing the vehicle; 'after' puts the insect last; 'to' is just a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtenant rents from a tenant, paying for part of the property let.

clue.text: Take care — stinger has been severed by struggle

indicators.note: the insect is cut apart with the other piece in the gap

parts.note: a bee is an insect with a sting
war is a struggle

explanation.surface: Watch out: a bee has been split in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been severed by' means the insect is split, the fight sitting in the gap between its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperative warning to watch out or be cautious.

clue.text: Note given to Warhol is sweet

parts.note: C is a musical note
Andy Warhol, the pop artist

explanation.surface: A note sent to the pop artist is charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy is the American word for sweets or confectionery.

clue.text: Profession for one tending to retain energy

indicators.note: the carer holds the other letter within

parts.note: a carer is someone who tends others
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A carer's job needs plenty of energy to be kept up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retain' puts E inside CARER.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is a person's working life or profession.

clue.text: Unsophisticated look to Weber before fight

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come in front of the fight

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
Wb is the symbol for the weber, the unit of magnetic flux
a row is a quarrel or fight

explanation.surface: A coarse glance at Weber before a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: Weber here is the SI unit, symbol Wb, not the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowbrow describes tastes that are unrefined or not intellectual.

clue.text: Flower sometimes needlessly gilded

parts.note: alludes to the saying about over-adorning something already beautiful, from Shakespeare's King John

explanation.walkthrough: To gild this flower is proverbially to embellish what needs no improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying about pointless gilding uses this white bloom as its example of perfection.

clue.text: Extend the prisoner's sentence

definitions.meaning: slang for a term of imprisonment

explanation.definitionFit: The word means lengthen and is also slang for a spell served in jail.

clue.text: Unhesitatingly, the qualified nurse is upset and takes a written examination

indicators.note: the remaining letters are knocked over, so rearranged
without er, the sound of hesitation, so those letters go

parts.note: a sister is a senior qualified nurse

explanation.surface: Without hesitation, the upset nurse sits a written test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unhesitatingly' drops ER from SISTER, leaving SIST; 'is upset' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit an exam is to take it, so one who sits takes a written test.

clue.text: Theatre cuts short words to popular song

indicators.note: the last letter is removed, shortening the word

parts.note: the words of a song are its lyrics

explanation.surface: A theatre trims the words of a pop song.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lyric is a West End theatre in London's Shaftesbury Avenue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lyric is the name of well-known theatres in London and elsewhere.

clue.text: Understand punter has to improve

parts.note: to get a joke is to understand it
a punter is someone who bets, a better

explanation.surface: Grasp that the gambler has to recover.
explanation.definitionFit: To get better is to recover or improve in health or quality.
